Likutay Halachos · Choshen Mishpat

Hilchos G'viyas Chov Min HaLikuchos V'Apotiki 1

Laws of Collecting a Debt from Purchasers and the Apotiki — 1 · Continuous essay · The lien upon land vs. movables, korban, s'michah, Yovel, and the kol

Even an explicit apotaiki — where he said to him: "You shall have no payment except from this" — it only takes effect upon land. And likewise a slave has a kol [voice/publicity] and his law is like that of land. But with mitaltelim — even if he made them an apotaiki, it is not effective, and the creditor may not seize them from the purchaser, for movables do not have a kol. See in the Shulchan Aruch these laws, for the essential lien is upon land.

Based on what was explained above in the preceding halachos, that the essential root of wealth is karka'os [land], and therefore they are more closely bound to the nefesh [soul], as above. And it has already been explained that the essential shi'bud [lien] is upon the body of the borrower himself, and on account of the lien upon himself, through this all his property becomes liened, as above.

And therefore the creditor seizes from the karka'os even from the hand of the purchaser. For the sale does not release from the lien that the lender has upon the borrower from his property. Because the karka'os are rooted in his soul more deeply, as above — therefore it is impossible to sell them completely and absolutely. And always there remains the inner dimension of their root — that is, the inner dimension of the root of the nefesh — with the seller.

And this is what we find: that at the time when the Yovel [Jubilee] was in force, it was impossible to sell land permanently, as it is written: "And the land shall not be sold permanently, for the land is Mine" (Leviticus 25:23). And it was in the power of the seller to redeem it after the sale, according to the law explicit in the Torah. And even if there was no redemption, it returned to him in the Yovel. But permanently and absolutely it is impossible to sell it at all.

And all of this is because the essential roots of the souls are there. And therefore they are rooted with the person more deeply. And therefore always there remains the inner dimension of their root with the seller of the field that is his from the inheritance of his fathers — for it is the essential nachalah [inheritance], for there are the roots of the souls, as above. And therefore it is impossible to sell it forever. And since the inner dimension of its root remains with him, therefore it is in his power to redeem it — for it has still not completely left his hand and domain, as above.

And therefore in the Yovel, when everything returns to its source and root — therefore the fields return to their owners then. For the inner dimension of their source and root remained with the seller, as above.

And therefore, since the karka'os always retain their root with the seller, and it is impossible to sell them completely — to remove them entirely together with the inner dimension of their root — therefore the lien of the creditor always remains upon them even after the sale. For the lien of the creditor is upon the body of the borrower himself, and the property is automatically liened, as above. And since in the aspect of the borrower himself there still remains with him the aspect of the inner dimension of the root of the landed property — therefore certainly the karka'os are automatically liened to the lender even after the sale, for their root still remains with the borrower. And the essential lien is upon the borrower, and the property is automatically liened, as above.

But the mitaltelim, which are in the aspect of peiros [fruits/produce] and are not so bound and rooted with him, as above — therefore the mitaltelim are sold with an absolute sale forever. For they immediately leave from domain to domain, because they are not so rooted with him, as above. And therefore the sale releases from the lien. For after the sale they immediately leave entirely from the domain of the seller.

And therefore they bear no lien of the lender at all. For the essential lien is upon the borrower himself, but the property — certainly the borrower has the right to sell them and give them and do with them as he wishes. Only at the time when the lender comes to collect the debt, if the borrower does not pay him, he collects from his property, which is liened to him on account of the borrower himself, as above. And since he preempted and sold them — and the sale of mitaltelim is an absolute sale, leaving his hand and domain entirely, as above — therefore the lien of the lender is released from them, and he has no lien upon them at all.

And even if he made them an apotaiki — nevertheless, the apotaiki is only a lien and is not an absolute sale, even an explicit apotaiki — for he can settle it with money. See in the Shulchan Aruch. And therefore the sale is greater, and releases the lien — for the sale of mitaltelim is an absolute sale, as above.

And this is the aspect of: Hekdeish, chameitz, and shichrur release from liens. And Hekdeish of monetary value does not release the lien — only sanctification of the body [k'dushas haguf]. For when one consecrates with sanctification of the body, through this the thing leaves his domain entirely, since the body has been sanctified, it is entirely forbidden to him.

For the sanctification of the body — that is, the aspect of a korban [offering], which he consecrates as an offering — and through the korban, the power of the inner dimension of the root of the soul of the animal, which is with the person, goes out. And this is the essential aspect of the korban: that he also offers up his own soul with the offering. And as is brought: that this is the essential aspect of the korban — that his soul should also ascend with it. And this is as above: for the korban is a person's property, where the root of his soul is. And when he raises and offers the korban, it emerges that his soul also ascends and is offered with it. In the aspect of: "From the animals, from the cattle... you shall offer your offering" (Leviticus 1:2) — "your offering" specifically, as is brought — that his soul also ascends with it, as above.

And this is the aspect of the s'michah [leaning of the hands upon the offering]. As it is written: "And he shall lean his hand upon it" (Leviticus 1:4) — "his hand" specifically. For there, [in the hands,] is the inner dimension of all the souls and spirits — in the aspect of: "In Your hand I entrust my spirit" (Psalms 31:6); in the aspect of: "In Whose hand is the soul of every living thing and the spirit of all human flesh" (Job 12:10) — as Rabbeinu, may his light shine, wrote in Siman 54 of Part 1. That is, the aspect of the ruach [spirit] is in the hands, as Rabbeinu, may his light shine, wrote several times. And the ruach is the inner dimension of the roots of the souls, as is known.

And this is the aspect of the s'michah, which is specifically with the hands — that is, he leans his hands upon the offering, and then he leans upon the offering also the aspect of the inner dimension of the soul, which is in the hands — where the aspect of ruach is, as above. And then he raises and offers also the inner dimension of the soul of the offering that was with him. And through this, his soul also ascends with the offering, as above.

segments.he: וע"כ כשהוא עני נמצא שנפגם חכמתו. וע"כ הוא נקרא בחי' בהמה שהוא העדר הדעת. כמו שאמר דוד (תהלים עג) ואני בער ולא אדע בהמות הייתי עמך. כי דוד היה קורא א"ע תמיד עני ואביון. כי היה עוסק תמיד בתפילתו לתקן מדה זו כידוע וזה שכתב רבינו ז"ל (סי' לז) שע"י צדקה נעשין בגדר אדם. כי זה מדה כנגד מדה ע"י שמעלה את העני מבהמה לאדם. ע"כ זוכה גם הוא שעולה לגדר אדם עי"ז. והדעת הוא בחי' סוכה כנ"ל. וסוכה הוא נוהגת ביום ובלילה כי הסוכה הוא בחי' ענני כבוד שכתוב בהם לא ימוש עמוד הענן יומם ועמוד האש לילה וכו'. כי עיקר הדעת הואבחי'חיבור חו"ג שהם בחי'יום ולילה. וסוכה הוא בחי' הדעת. וע"כ עמוד הענן משלים וכו'. כי עיקר הדעת שהיא בחי' סוכה בחי' ענני כבוד הוא בחי' חיבור יום ולילה כנ"ל וע"כ צריכין להשיב את העבוט ביום ובלילה. דהיינו כסות יום ביום וכו'. כדי להשלים ולחבר יום ולילה כדי לתקן את הדעת של העני. כי עיקר תיקון העניות הוא ע"י חיבור יום ולילה כידוע. שזהו בחי' שלימות הדעת כנ"ל. כי הממון דקדושה הוא שלימות הנפש. כי הנפש שרשה בממון וצריך להשתדל עם העני להשלים נפשו ודעתו כדי שיצא מעניות לעשירות. כ"ש והחזקת בו ע"י הלוואה. כ"ש שם אל תקח מאתו נשך וכו'. כי צריכין להחזיק בידו וכו': (כל זה לא נכתב בשלימות רק בקיצור ראשי פרקים. כי לא נכתב בזמנו. ונשכח רובו ככולו):
segments.en:
It emerges that the korban, which is sanctification of the body — then he consecrates and removes from his hand also the inner dimension of the root of the soul, as above. And therefore it releases from the lien — since there remains with the borrower no root or connection at all, as above.

And this is the aspect of shichrur [emancipation], which also releases from liens. For slaves are equated to land. And therefore the lien of the apotaiki takes effect upon them also, and if he sold them [the creditor] seizes from the hand of the purchaser, as is ruled in the Shulchan Aruch. For a slave is similar to a woman — for he is obligated in the mitzvos in which a woman is obligated. And therefore he is similar to land, in the aspect of ishah, karka, olam [woman, land, world], as Rabbeinu wrote this hint elsewhere.

And therefore it is impossible to release the slave except through a get shichrur [writ of emancipation], like a woman through a get k'risus [writ of severance/divorce]. For the get shichrur is in the aspect of the get k'risus. As it says in the Mishnah: in several ways the get is comparable to the shichrur. That is: because the slave is the aspect of karka and is rooted in his soul more deeply — therefore it is impossible to release him except through a get shichrur, that is, through a writing, through which the inner dimension of the soul goes out. And as was explained above in Hilchos Halva'ah, the aspect of the get, which is specifically through writing, see there.

And therefore the shichrur also releases from liens — since through the shichrur he also removes the inner dimension of the soul, through which the lien is released, as above. And likewise chameitz and other things from which benefit is forbidden also release from liens, as is ruled in the Shulchan Aruch — since they leave his domain entirely and he retains no benefit from them whatsoever. Therefore the lien is also released, as above.

And this is the aspect of what our Sages, zichronam livrachah, said regarding this matter: that the reason is that karka'os, and likewise a slave, have a kol [voice/publicity], and therefore the lien of the apotaiki is effective upon them. But mitaltelim do not have a kol. For the kol is the aspect of the ruach, as is known — which is the aspect of the inner dimension of the root of the soul, as above. And therefore the karka'os, which are the essential root of the soul — and likewise the slave, who is similar to a woman, who is the essential aspect of the soul, the aspect of wealth — therefore they have a kol. For the kol is always close to dibur [speech] — which is the aspect of ruach and nefesh. And since they are the essential root of the soul, therefore the kol, which is the aspect of the ruach, which is the aspect of the inner dimension of the root of the soul, is close to them — for the kol is the inner dimension of their root, as above. And therefore they have a kol.

But mitaltelim, which are branches of the root and are not so close to the kol — therefore they do not have a kol. And therefore the lien does not take effect upon them, as above.

And therefore in the Yovel, through the kol shofar [voice of the shofar], the fields return — and likewise other things [do not return] to their root except in the Yovel, which is the aspect of the root of all the souls. And this is revealed through the kol, which is the aspect of the inner dimension of the roots of the souls, as above. Therefore then they all return to their root through the kol shofar, as above.

The meaning of apotaiki: apo t'hai ka'i — "upon this it shall stand." For the money is the aspect of regel [foot], which is the aspect of standing. As our Sages, zichronam livrachah, said (Pesachim 119a): "And all the wealth [y'kum] that was at their feet" (Deuteronomy 11:6) — this is a person's money, which stands him upon his feet. And this is apo t'hai ka'i: "from here shall be your money," which is the aspect of his feet, as above.

Summary of G'viyas Chov Min HaLikuchos V'Apotiki 1

Continuous essay (no osiyos, 9,666 Hebrew chars). Core framework: Why the creditor's shi'bud applies to karka'os even after sale to a purchaser, but not to mitaltelim.

Karka'os = ikkar shoresh ha'ashirus = nisrashin b'nafsho b'yoser → sale is never absolute (p'nimiyus shorshan remains with seller). Proof: in Yovel era, land cannot be sold litz'misus ("v'ha'aretz lo simachair litz'misus ki Li ha'aretz," Vayikra 25:23). Therefore ba'al chov toreif from karka'os even miyad halokai'ach (lien persists through sale).

Mitaltelim = b'chinas peiros, not so rooted → sale is absolute → teichef yotz'in meirshus lirshus → shi'bud nifka. Even apotaiki m'forash doesn't help (apotaiki = only shi'bud, not m'chirah g'murah).

Hekdeish chameitz v'shichrur mafki'in midei shi'bud: Only k'dushas haguf (not Hekdeish damim) releases, because korban removes p'nimiyus shoresh hanefesh. Explained through s'michah: "v'samach es yado alav" (Vayikra 1:4) — the yad holds p'nimiyus kol han'fashos v'haruchos ("b'yad'cha afkid ruchi," T'hilim 31:6; "asher b'yado nefesh kol chai," Iyov 12:10 — as per LM I:54). Through s'michah, p'nimiyus nefesh ascends with korban → fully exits his r'shus → shi'bud released.

Shichrur: avadim hukshu l'karka'os. Slave = domeh l'ishah (chayav b'mitzvos sh'ha'ishah chayeves) → b'chinas ishah/karka/olam. Freed only through get shichrur (= get k'risus) because rooted in nefesh → removes p'nimiyus → releases shi'bud. Chameitz/isurei hana'ah: motzi'o l'gamrei meirshuso → mafkia.

Kol: Karka'os and eved yeish lahem kol = b'chinas ruach = p'nimiyus shoresh hanefesh (kol = samuch l'dibur always = ruach v'nefesh). Mitaltelim = anfei hashoresh → ain lahem kol → ain shi'bud. In Yovel: through kol shofar → fields return (shofar = reveals p'nimiyus shorshei han'fashos).

Apotiki = "apo t'hai ka'i" (here it shall stand). Mamon = b'chinas regel/amidah: "v'es kol hay'kum asher b'raglaihem = mamono shel adam shema'amido al raglav" (Pesachim 119a; D'varim 11:6).
